editorial:
Imagine being a bored housewife who suddenly decides to rob a department store just for the thrill of it. That is exactly what happens to Mikako, and it kicks off a wild ride. She steals a gold bell and realizes she has a real talent for crime, which wakes up her childhood dream of being special. The vibe is light and funny, but it gets messy fast. You get to watch her go from a quiet home life to planning a massive heist for a tea bowl worth billions. It is a chaotic mix of greed and family drama that keeps you guessing.

What really makes this work is the chemistry between Mikako and Kinjo, the guy trying to use her for his own gain. The twists are surprising, and the way her husband gets dragged into the crime while dealing with his own cheating scandal is just gold. It is fast and fun, though some parts of the plot feel a bit rushed.
endingExplained: In the end, Mikako pulls off the big heist but realizes the gold was never the real prize. She manages to outsmart Kinjo, leaving him with nothing while she secures her freedom. Her husband finally stops his cheating and they find a strange new bond through their shared crime. They don't end up rich, but they are no longer bored. It wraps up with a funny scene showing her looking for her next big target.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heist movies with a comedic twist and quirky characters.
